title: Roos triangle for the actual derived reduction sections
statement: Fix $\ell,E,U,\Gamma,R\Gamma$ as in [def-sfb-complete-reduction-sections-model]. Let $K\in D(\mathcal M)$, $P$ be K-flat, and $e:Q(P)\simeq K$. Let $I$ be K-injective in complexes of strict module towers and $j:T(P)\to I$ a strict map from the actual tensor-reduction tower, each $j_n$ a quasi-isomorphism. Then $Q\operatorname{Roos}(\Gamma^{\mathrm{Tow}}I)$ is a derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of $R\Gamma(K_n)$, with transitions $R\Gamma$ of the actual canonical integral transitions of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. The product in the Roos triangle is any fixed categorical product; no completeness or vanishing hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D6K, lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim; Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim; Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok

proof.text: Evaluation of a K-injective strict tower is K-injective. Thus ordinary sections of each I_n compute derived sections. The pointwise quasi-isomorphisms j_n and the scalar-extension computation on K-flat P give isomorphisms Q(Γ I_n) ≅ RΓ(K_n). Naturality of j and the scalar comparison makes these isomorphisms commute with all actual quotient transitions.

Exact countable products in abelian groups identify the localized termwise product of Γ I_n with its derived product. The inverse rotation of the mapping-cone triangle defining the strict Roos fibre is distinguished. Transport both product vertices by the product of the level isomorphisms. Their transition compatibility identifies the second arrow with one minus shift for the canonical reduction section tower. This is the defining derived-limit triangle.

theorem reduction_sections_roos_triangle
    (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E U))
    (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E U) ℤ)
    (hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (AdicCompletion.Modules l E U) (.up ℤ)).kFlat P)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K)
    (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AdicCompletion.Modules l E U) ℤ)
    (hI : I.IsKInjective)
    (j : Functor.ofOpSequence
      (X := fun n : ℕ ↦ (AdicCompletion.level l E U n).obj P)
      (AdicCompletion.levelStep l E U P) ⟶ I.asFunctor)
    (hj : ∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (j.app (op n)))
    [HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦
      (rgamma l E U).obj (AdicCompletion.integralLevel l E U K n))] :
    IsDerivedLimit (K := fun n : ℕ ↦
      (rgamma l E U).obj (AdicCompletion.integralLevel l E U K n))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (rgamma l E U).map (AdicCompletion.integralStep l E U K n))
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (roosF.obj (sectionTower l E U I)))
